exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated routing protocols allow an attacker to inject false routing updates and intercept or redirect traffic, enabling adversary-in-the-middle attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DHCP Spoofing
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of authentication in dynamic routing protocols is analogous to spoofing-based AitM techniques where an attacker injects malicious routing information to redirect network traffic.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Exploiting weak BGP authentication can allow an attacker to manipulate routing tables and bridge or bypass network boundaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak BGP authentication may expose session credentials and routing data to network sniffing attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Password Guessing
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted management plane access exposes the device to brute-force password guessing attacks against administrative interfaces.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted management plane access allows attackers to leverage remote service protocols (SSH, Telnet, etc.) to compromise the device.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credential Stuffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Open management plane access enables credential stuffing attacks using previously compromised credentials against management interfaces.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Device Configuration Dump
exploitedBy.relevance: Cleartext protocols allow attackers to capture and extract full device configurations transmitted in plaintext.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Device Authentication
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak credentials on network devices directly relate to subverting network device authentication mechanisms.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Password Cracking
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or default passwords are easily cracked offline if hashed credentials are obtained from the device configuration.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol Tunneling
exploitedBy.relevance: Without prefix list filtering, attackers can advertise routes that facilitate tunneling traffic through unintended network paths.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Hide Infrastructure
exploitedBy.relevance: Absent route filtering can allow adversaries to inject routes that obscure or hide malicious infrastructure within the routing domain.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Valid Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessively privileged operator accounts, if compromised, provide attackers with valid high-privilege access to network infrastructure.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Account Manipulation
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive privileges allow an attacker who gains access to manipulate accounts and maintain or escalate their access on the device.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Indicator Blocking
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient logging of routing changes prevents detection of malicious route modifications, effectively blocking indicators of compromise.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Clear Network Connection History and Configurations
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of routing change logs mirrors the impact of an attacker clearing network history, leaving no audit trail for unauthorized routing modifications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Unpatched routing software contains known vulnerabilities that can be exploited remotely to compromise the device.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Patch System Image
exploitedBy.relevance: Unpatched firmware is directly related to system image integrity; attackers may also modify firmware when patch management is absent.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
exploitedBy.relevance: Known vulnerabilities in unpatched routing software can be exploited to gain elevated privileges on the device.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: SNMP (MIB Dump)
exploitedBy.relevance: Exposed SNMP community strings directly enable attackers to perform MIB dumps and extract sensitive device configuration and network topology data.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: OS Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Without control plane policing, an attacker can flood the router CPU with crafted packets, exhausting OS resources and causing denial of service.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Endpoint Denial of Service
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing control plane policing leaves network devices vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks targeting the control plane processor.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Hardcoded routing credentials stored in configuration files are directly equivalent to credentials stored in files, easily extracted by attackers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Private Keys
exploitedBy.relevance: Hardcoded credentials may include private keys or shared secrets embedded in configuration files that can be extracted and reused by attackers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Multi-hop Proxy
exploitedBy.relevance: IP source routing can be abused to force packets through attacker-controlled hops, effectively creating a multi-hop proxy for traffic redirection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: System Time Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated NTP exposes time synchronization data and can be abused to discover or manipulate system time for further attacks.
